R0257.title: C2C Cash-on-Delivery Abandonment
R0257.definition: In C2C cash-on-delivery scenarios, recipients deliberately refuse or abandon parcels, shifting freight and goods losses onto senders or the platform.
R0257.description:
C2C COD abandonment occurs when recipients deliberately refuse or abandon parcels in cash-on-delivery C2C trades, shifting round-trip freight and goods losses onto senders or the platform, often for harassment, fraud, or competitor disruption.

The risk causes round-trip freight, goods damage, and warehousing costs and undermines C2C trust. Detection must combine recipient refusal history, address risk, and COD order behavior models to restrict and verify high-frequency abandoners.
R0257.influence: COD abandonment causes round-trip freight, goods damage, and warehousing losses, raises dispute handling costs, and undermines C2C COD availability.

references.title: Large COD Order Rejected Causing Merchant Loss (CNR, C2C COD Abandonment)

observables: C2C cash-on-delivery recipients frequently refuse or abandon parcels
Refusal rates for the same recipient or address are markedly higher than the average
COD abandonment is accompanied by malicious-retaliation or competitor-harassment signatures
Round-trip shipping and goods-loss costs are concentrated on senders or the platform
Anomalous abandonment clusters appear in the COD order behavior model
